difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the normalization of a scheme by two properties: that it is integral and birational over the base, and that any integral birational morphism from a normal scheme factors uniquely through it. The proof first constructs the factorisation for an integral birational morphism using the affine equivalence between algebras and quasi-coherent sheaves and the corresponding uniqueness in the affine case, then derives from the existence of such factorisations that the normalisation is itself normal, and finally records the uniqueness of the factorisation on the level of the rings.
